Hi team —

Quick answer: we can treat the $10k as a promotional sponsorship (marketing expense) and issue per-winner promo codes. Guidance and operational checklist below: 

1) Documentation we need from HackFast: a sponsorship acceptance letter or PO that includes their legal entity name and EIN. If the recipient will not invoice us (they are the beneficiary of credits), we dont need a W9 from them to issue credits. However, if HackFast plans to invoice Redwood for services tied to the event, we will need a vendor W9.

2) Tax treatment: credits issued for marketing/prize purposes are not a Redwood taxable revenue event. For the recipient, the fair market value of credits could be taxable; thats their responsibility. We should include a short disclaimer in the sponsor letter stating credits may have tax implications for recipients and recommend they consult tax advisors.

3) Internal controls / ledger: create entry as Marketing Promo Expense > Program: HackFast 2026. Tag cost center 4102 and set effective date of issuance. 

4) Expiry + packaging: 12-month expiry is fine. For tracking and ease, issue per-winner promo codes (unique, single-use) and record each code in the attached ledger template. We'll also store the promo code batch in our billing system with ledger reference HS-2389.

5) Approval path: Marketing lead sign-off (Marissa) + Finance acknowledgement (this email thread) + Ops to confirm code generation.

Ive attached our short internal process doc and a W9 request template in case the external party becomes a vendor: [Attachment: promo-credit-process.pdf, W9_request_template.txt]. Ben, if you want to keep it simpler from ops, we can batch-generate 25 single-use codes and hand them to Sarah.

Marissa — once you confirm, Finance will create the ledger entry and well queue the promo code batch for issuance.

Laura Bennett
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
